cards.name: LexGuard
cards.lede: Makes contract risks easier to inspect before signing. A staged agent pipeline examines clauses, checks explicit traps, **verifies every statute it cites** and proposes rewrites.
cards.notes: A deterministic auditor runs hand-written trap patterns before any agent reads a risk level, and it can force an escalation: LLMs under-rate predatory clauses written in calm legal language. Citations are looked up and graded against a statute database. Providers fail mid-document, so the AI client falls through Gemini, Groq, Hugging Face, Grok and local Ollama. PDFs are repaired by a two-pass chunker before any model sees them, and clauses are keyed by position because LLM-echoed IDs drifted. It runs inside 512 MB: a 380 MB V8 heap cap, idle models unloaded, GC after each job.

cards.name: Pikina
cards.lede: An offline-first Windows/Linux assistant with local inference, validated tools and **consent for anything high-risk**.
cards.notes: Known intents go through a regex router with no model call; everything else goes to a local model through Ollama. Every proposed action is schema-checked against a capability registry. One consent rule covers every entry point: level 4 always asks, and level 3 asks when the action can't be rolled back. Multi-step plans run as transactions and roll back step by step when one fails.

cards.name: Noesis
cards.lede: Finds the useful moment across a pile of mixed media. Video, audio, PDFs and images go in; **every answer links to a timestamp or page**.
cards.notes: Each source becomes a SuperChunk that keeps its time window or page. Dense (ChromaDB) and sparse (BM25) results are merged with reciprocal rank fusion, a local cross-encoder reranks them, and a separate fact-audit pass labels every claim in the answer as supported, partially supported or unsupported.

cards.name: Mobius
cards.tag: BILLING · POSTGRES INVARIANTS · with Apurva Patil
cards.lede: Runs the whole life of a subscription, from quotation to recurring invoices and payments, and **the database itself enforces that billing is correct**.
cards.notes: Quotation → confirmation → activation → recurring invoices → payments → reports, across an admin console, a staff workspace and a customer portal, with product variants, GST, discount campaigns and four billing cadences. A `UNIQUE (subscription_id, period_start)` constraint plus `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` means re-runs and parallel runs cannot double-bill; each subscription is locked `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; a catch-up loop bills every period missed during downtime; and a discount slot is claimed with one conditional `UPDATE`, so two invoices can never take the last one. Money is computed to the paisa.

claims.label: idempotent insert

claims.needle: FOR UPDATE OF s SKIP LOCKED
claims.label: parallel-safe lock

cards.name: BenchShield
cards.tag: AI EVALUATION · SECURITY · with Rudra Patel
cards.lede: Finds where an AI benchmark's questions and answers have leaked onto the web, and **backs every finding with pinned, human-reviewed evidence**.
cards.notes: Benchmarks lose their value once their answers leak, because browsing agents can look them up instead of solving the task. BenchShield keeps four steps apart (discovery, verification, agent experiments and human review) so a promising search hit can never become an unsupported contamination claim. Protected answers live in a vault encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Long-running work runs on a durable PostgreSQL worker with leases, heartbeats and fencing tokens, and every major design choice is written down as an architecture decision record.

claims.needle: Durable PostgreSQL-backed job worker with heartbeats, leases, and fencing tokens.
claims.label: durable worker

claims.needle: Claim next pending or expired task using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with fencing token bump.
claims.label: fenced task claim

cards.name: Resilion
cards.lede: Turns supply-chain news into structured risk events and **traces which industries get hit**.
cards.notes: Gemini extracts events from articles; validators reject any event type, severity or trade corridor the graph doesn't already know, so the model can't invent a place. Graph traversal then walks from the disrupted corridor to the refineries and industries downstream and scores their exposure.

cards.notes: Tickets route to the right staff member automatically. ETAs come from simulating that person's whole open queue rather than a fixed SLA, a late ticket tells the student why it is late, and a background job escalates anything past its deadline.

cards.name: ShopKart
cards.lede: A store whose checkout **never trusts the browser with a price**.
cards.notes: The server rebuilds every order from database prices and live stock, and an order is marked paid only after Razorpay's signature checks out with HMAC-SHA256 on the server.

cards.name: C++ Shell
cards.lede: A shell built on **fork, exec, pipe and dup2**: quoting, redirection, pipelines and background jobs.
cards.notes: Builtins, PATH lookup, a quoting state machine for single and double quotes, I/O redirection and multi-stage pipelines. Each stage's stdin is rewired to the previous stage's pipe with dup2, and every unused pipe end is closed so the next stage sees EOF.

cards.name: Meta OpenEnv
cards.lede: An environment where agents juggle assignments, bugs and deadlines, and **finishing by burning out still loses points**.
cards.notes: Built for the Meta PyTorch OpenEnv Hackathon. An agent schedules work against hard deadlines across easy, medium and hard tasks; the graders reward finished work and add bonuses only for burnout-free days (none over 8 hours) and balanced schedules.
